1.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
1.solution:
For a vehicle on a curved road the normal reaction depends on the centripetal requirement.
Horizontal: \(N = mg\).
Convex (centre below): \(mg - N = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow N = mg - \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} < mg\).
Concave (centre above): \(N - mg = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow N = mg + \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} > mg\).
Hence the normal reaction is maximum on the concave road.

2.solution:
Each alpha emission reduces mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2; each beta emission increases atomic number by 1 (mass number unchanged).
Mass: \(226 - 206 = 20 = 4\times(\text{no. of }\alpha)\Rightarrow\) number of \(\alpha = 5\).
Atomic number after 5 \(\alpha\): \(88 - 10 = 78\). To reach 82: \(82 - 78 = 4\) beta particles.
So 5 alpha and 4 beta.

3.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
3.solution:
Distance between 1st and 10th maxima \(= 9\omega = (16.75 - 14.50) = 2.25\) mm, so fringe width \(\omega = 0.25\) mm.
New fringe width \(\omega' = \dfrac{5500}{6000}\times0.25 = 0.229\) mm (\(\omega\propto\lambda\)).
The central (zero order) maximum position is unchanged: \(y_{0} = y_{1} - \omega = 14.50 - 0.25 = 14.25\) mm.
Tenth order: \(y_{10} = y_{0} + 10\omega' = 14.25 + 10\times0.229 = 16.54\approx16.55\) mm.

4.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
4.solution:
Phosphorus is a donor, making the silicon n-type with \(n_{e}\approx10^{21}/m^{3}\). Mass-action law: \(n_{e}n_{h} = n_{i}^{2}\).
\[n_{h} = \frac{n_{i}^{2}}{n_{e}} = \frac{(10^{16})^{2}}{10^{21}} = \frac{10^{32}}{10^{21}} = 10^{11}/m^{3}.\]

5.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
5.solution:
For a conical/banking situation the bob hangs at angle \(\theta\) with \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^{2}}{rg}\).
\[\tan\theta = \frac{(10)^{2}}{20\times10} = \frac{100}{200} = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.5).\]

6.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
6.solution:
Limit of resolution of the eye (treating the pupil as an aperture) gives angular resolution \(\Delta\theta = \dfrac{1.22\lambda}{D}\) where \(D = 2\times0.25 = 0.5\) cm is the pupil diameter. Minimum separation at distance \(L = 25\) cm:
\[\Delta x = L\,\Delta\theta = \frac{1.22\lambda L}{D} = \frac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}\times0.25}{0.5\times10^{-2}} \approx 3\times10^{-5}\ \text{m} = 30\ \mu\text{m}.\]

7.solution:
By Gauss's law the net flux depends only on the net enclosed charge: \(\phi = \dfrac{q_{net}}{\varepsilon_{0}}\).
Net charge \(= 2 - 3 + 4 - 4 - 1 = -2\ \mu\text{C}\), so the flux is \(\dfrac{-2\,\mu\text{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}\), and among the printed options the keyed one corresponds to a net charge of \(-2\,\mu\text{C}\).
7.note: Stem lists charges as 2, -3, 4, -4, -1 microC giving net -2 microC. The option set is garbled (mixes flux q/epsilon0 forms with a bare charge '-2 microC'); the keyed option B encodes the correct net charge -2 microC, so kept as printed.

8.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
8.solution:
Sphere about diameter: \(I_{s} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^{2}\); cylinder about axis: \(I_{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^{2}\). Given \(\omega_{c} = 2\omega_{s}\).
\[\frac{E_{s}}{E_{c}} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}I_{s}\omega_{s}^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}I_{c}\omega_{c}^{2}} = \frac{\frac{2}{5}mR^{2}\,\omega_{s}^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}mR^{2}\,(2\omega_{s})^{2}} = \frac{\frac{2}{5}}{\frac{1}{2}\times4} = \frac{2/5}{2} = \frac{1}{5}.\]

9.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
9.solution:
First echo: distance to nearer cliff \(= \dfrac{vt_{1}}{2} = \dfrac{340\times1}{2} = 170\) m.
Second echo: distance to farther cliff \(= \dfrac{vt_{2}}{2} = \dfrac{340\times3}{2} = 510\) m.
Distance between cliffs \(= 170 + 510 = 680\) m.

10.solution:
Series of 10 capacitors \(C_{1}\): \(C_{s} = \dfrac{C_{1}}{10}\), charged to 4V, energy \(E_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_{1}}{10}(4V)^{2}\).
Parallel of 8 capacitors \(C_{2}\): \(C_{p} = 8C_{2}\), charged to V, energy \(E_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(8C_{2})V^{2}\).
Setting \(E_{1}=E_{2}\): \(\dfrac{C_{1}}{10}\times16 = 8C_{2}\Rightarrow C_{2} = \dfrac{16C_{1}}{80} = \dfrac{C_{1}}{5}.\)

11.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
11.solution:
Same mass and same material; solid sphere is more compact (smaller radius) but the standard comparison at equal mass and radius gives \(I_{s} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2}\) and \(I_{h} = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^{2}\).
\[\frac{I_{s}}{I_{h}} = \frac{2/5}{2/3} = \frac{3}{5} < 1 \Rightarrow I_{h} > I_{s}.\]
The hollow sphere has mass distributed farther from the axis, so \(I_{h} > I_{s}\).

12.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
12.solution: Induced charge \(q = \displaystyle\int i\,dt = \int\frac{1}{R}\frac{d\phi}{dt}dt = \frac{\Delta\phi}{R}\). It depends on the total change in magnetic flux (and resistance), not on the rate of change.

13.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
13.solution:
A liquid film has two surfaces, so work done \(= T\times2\Delta A\).
\(A_{1} = 5\times4 = 20\ \text{cm}^{2}\), \(A_{2} = 7\times8 = 56\ \text{cm}^{2}\), \(\Delta A = 36\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^{2}\).
\[T = \frac{W}{2\Delta A} = \frac{3\times10^{-4}}{2\times36\times10^{-4}} = \frac{3}{72} \approx 0.04\ \text{N/m}.\]

14.solution:
Kelvin reading \(x\) means Celsius \(= x - 273\). Fahrenheit \(= \dfrac{9}{5}(x-273) + 32\). Set equal to \(x\):
\[x = \frac{9}{5}(x-273) + 32 \Rightarrow x - 32 = \frac{9}{5}(x-273) \Rightarrow 5x - 160 = 9x - 2457 \Rightarrow 4x = 2297 \Rightarrow x = 574.25 \approx 574.\]
14.note: Filed under Thermal Properties (temperature-scale conversion); no dedicated scale subtopic exists, closest thermal subtopic used.

15.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
15.solution:
Capillary rise \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g} \propto \dfrac{1}{g}\). With \(g_{m} = \dfrac{g_{e}}{6}\):
\[\frac{h_{m}}{h_{e}} = \frac{g_{e}}{g_{m}} = 6 \Rightarrow h_{m} = 6h_{e}.\]
The rise on the moon is six times that on the earth.

16.subtopic: Lenses — Lens Formula, Power, and Lensmaker
16.solution: For two thin lenses in contact \(P = P_{1} + P_{2} = \dfrac{1}{f_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{f_{2}}\). With the simplified relation \(f\propto R\) used here, taking each focal length proportional to its radius, the combined power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{f_{2}} \propto \dfrac{1}{R_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{R_{2}} = \dfrac{R_{1}+R_{2}}{R_{1}R_{2}}\).

17.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
17.solution: By kinetic theory the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is \(\dfrac{3}{2}kT\), which depends only on temperature. At a given temperature this average kinetic energy is the same for all molecules (velocity and momentum differ because masses differ).

18.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
18.solution: In a common-emitter amplifier the output (collector) voltage is \(180^\circ\) out of phase with the input (base) voltage, i.e. a phase difference of \(\pi\) radians.

19.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
19.solution:
Restoring (spring) force provides the centripetal force on the mass at radius \((L+x)\): \(kx = m(L+x)\omega^{2}\).
With \(k = 8\ \text{N/m}\), \(m = 0.1\) kg, \(\omega = 8\) rad/s:
\[8x = 0.1\times64\times(L+x) = 6.4(L+x) \Rightarrow 8x - 6.4x = 6.4L \Rightarrow 1.6x = 6.4L \Rightarrow \frac{x}{L} = 4:1.\]
19.note: Stem dropped the spring constant value ('spring constant N/m'); from the AK working it is 8 N/m.
19.stemOverride: A body of mass 100 gram is tied to a spring of spring constant \(8\text{ }N/m\), while the other end of a spring is fixed. If the body moves in a circular path on smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed \(8rad/s\) then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be

20.solution:
Full-scale current of the voltmeter: \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{10}{50} = 0.2\) A.
To extend the range to 15 V a series resistance \(R'\) is required: \(R + R' = \dfrac{V'}{I}\Rightarrow 50 + R' = \dfrac{15}{0.2} = 75\Rightarrow R' = 25\ \Omega\) in series.

21.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
21.solution:
Incident heat splits into absorbed + reflected + transmitted: \(Q = Q_{a} + Q_{r} + Q_{t}\).
Absorbed \(= 0.6\times120 = 72\) J, transmitted \(= 12\) J.
\[Q_{r} = 120 - 72 - 12 = 36\ \text{J}.\]

22.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
22.solution:
Field at centre of a coil of \(n\) turns: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}nI}{2r}\Rightarrow n = \dfrac{2Br}{\mu_{0}I}\).
\[n = \frac{2\times3.14\times10^{-4}\times8\times10^{-2}}{12.56\times10^{-7}\times0.4} = \frac{5.024\times10^{-5}}{5.024\times10^{-7}} = 100.\]
22.note: Stem dropped the leading digit of the field; from the AK working B = 3.14 x 10^-4 T.
22.stemOverride: A circular coil of wire consisting of ' \(n\) ' turns each of radius 8 cm carries a current of 0.4 A . The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of coil is \(3.14 \times10^{- 4}\text{ }T\). The value of ' n ' is [Take \(\mu_{0}= 12.56 \times10^{- 7}\) SI unit]

23.solution:
Efflux speeds: \(v_{1} = \sqrt{2g(h+x)}\) (lower hole, depth \(h+x\)) and \(v_{2} = \sqrt{2gx}\) (upper hole, depth \(x\)). Thrust from each jet \(= \rho A v^{2}\), so net horizontal force:
\[F = \rho A(v_{1}^{2} - v_{2}^{2}) = \rho A[2g(h+x) - 2gx] = 2\rho A g h \propto h.\]

24.solution: From the graph the lines give \(V = Q/C\), so the line with smaller slope has larger capacitance. For the same charge \(Q\), \(V_{A} < V_{B}\) (line A lies below line B). Hence \(C_{A} = Q/V_{A} > Q/V_{B} = C_{B}\): capacitor A has the higher capacitance.

26.subtopic: Magnetisation, Susceptibility, Permeability, and B-H-M Relations
26.solution: A paramagnetic substance has a small positive susceptibility (\(0 < \chi \ll 1\)). So it is positive and small.

27.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
27.solution:
At constant pressure the fraction of heat used as external work is \(\dfrac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} = \dfrac{R}{C_{p}} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}\).
With \(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\): \(1 - \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4 = 40\%\).

28.solution: When the galvanometer current is zero, no current flows through the 6 V branch, so R carries the full loop current driven by the 10 V cell through the \(4\,\Omega\) resistor, and the potential drop across R must balance the 6 V cell: \(V_{R} = 6\) V. Current through the \(4\,\Omega\): \(i = \dfrac{10 - 6}{4} = 1\) A. This same current passes through R, so \(R = \dfrac{V_{R}}{i} = \dfrac{6}{1} = 6\,\Omega\).

29.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
29.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
29.solution:
Einstein's equation \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \phi + eV\):
\[\frac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = \phi + eV_{1}\ \ (i),\qquad \frac{hc}{3\lambda_{1}} = \phi + \frac{eV_{1}}{6}\ \ (ii).\]
Multiply (ii) by 6: \(\dfrac{2hc}{\lambda_{1}} = 6\phi + eV_{1}\) (iii). Subtract (i) from (iii): \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = 5\phi\). Since \(\phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{0}}\), \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{5hc}{\lambda_{0}}\Rightarrow \lambda_{0} = 5\lambda_{1}.\)

30.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats

31.solution: Three equal capacitors in series: \(\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{3}{C}\Rightarrow C_{eq} = \dfrac{C}{3}\). In series the same charge gives equal voltage across each, so the combination withstands \(V + V + V = 3V\) before breakdown. Hence \(\dfrac{C}{3},\ 3V\).

32.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
32.solution:
Power factor \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow \phi = 30^\circ\). For an L-R series circuit \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{\omega L}{R}\):
\[L = \frac{R\tan30^\circ}{\omega} = \frac{50\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{2\pi\times50} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}\,\pi}\ \text{H}\quad(f = 50\ \text{Hz}).\]

33.subtopic: Variation of g with Depth, Altitude, Density, and Latitude

34.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
34.solution:
The two straight radial portions through O contribute zero field. Each semicircle gives \(B = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{4R}\) at the centre. The currents in the two semicircles circulate oppositely, so the net field is the difference:
\[B_{net} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R_{2}} - \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R_{1}} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4}\left[\frac{1}{R_{2}} - \frac{1}{R_{1}}\right].\]

35.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
35.solution:
\(\overrightarrow{F} = (t\widehat{i} + 2t^{2}\widehat{j})\), \(m = 1\) kg, so \(\overrightarrow{a} = \overrightarrow{F}\). Velocity from rest: \(\overrightarrow{v} = \int\overrightarrow{a}\,dt = \dfrac{t^{2}}{2}\widehat{i} + \dfrac{2t^{3}}{3}\widehat{j}\).
Power \(P = \overrightarrow{F}\cdot\overrightarrow{v} = t\cdot\dfrac{t^{2}}{2} + 2t^{2}\cdot\dfrac{2t^{3}}{3} = \dfrac{t^{3}}{2} + \dfrac{4t^{5}}{3}\).
At \(t = 3\): \(P = \dfrac{27}{2} + \dfrac{4\times243}{3} = 13.5 + 324 = 337.5\) W.

36.solution:
\(g = \dfrac{4\pi^{2}l}{T^{2}}\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta g}{g} = \dfrac{\Delta l}{l} + 2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}\).
\(\dfrac{\Delta l}{l} = \dfrac{1\,\text{mm}}{1000\,\text{mm}} = 0.1\%\). Total time of 100 oscillations \(= 200\) s, least count 0.1 s, so \(\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = \dfrac{0.1}{200} = 0.05\%\).
\[\frac{\Delta g}{g} = 0.1\% + 2\times0.05\% = 0.2\%.\]

37.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
37.solution: In a centre-tap full-wave rectifier the secondary is divided by the centre tap; each diode handles half the secondary voltage, so the output with respect to each diode is \(\dfrac{1}{2}V_{s}\).
37.note: Option C text is garbled ('V_n') in extraction; it denotes (1/2)V_s, the keyed and correct value.

u = R\left(\dfrac{1}{n_{f}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{n_{i}^{2}}ight)\).

39.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
39.solution: Open-pipe fundamental is 80 Hz, so \(\dfrac{v}{2L} = 80\Rightarrow \dfrac{v}{L} = 160\). Closing one end gives fundamental \(\dfrac{v}{4L} = 40\) Hz, and a closed pipe produces only odd harmonics: \(40, 120, 200, 280, \dots\)

40.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
40.solution:
Maximum current at resonance: \(X_{L} = X_{C}\Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi^{2}f^{2}L}\).
\[C = \frac{1}{4\times10\times(50)^{2}\times2.5} = \frac{1}{4\times10\times2500\times2.5} = 4\times10^{-6}\ \text{F} = 4\ \mu\text{F}.\]
At resonance \(I_{max} = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{230}{11.5} = 20\) A.

41.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
41.solution: Zero specific heat means no heat exchange \(\Rightarrow\) adiabatic process, for which \(PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}\). Comparing with \(PV^{n} = \text{constant}\) gives \(n = \gamma\).

42.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
42.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
42.solution: Saturation current is proportional to the number of photoelectrons emitted per second, which increases with the intensity of incident light. (Maximum KE depends on frequency, not intensity; the effect needs the particle/photon theory; stopping potential depends on frequency and work function.) Correct statement: saturation current increases with intensity.

43.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
43.solution:
\(y = 60\sin(1200t - 6x)\) micron: amplitude \(a = 60\,\mu\text{m}\), \(\omega = 1200\), \(k = 6\).
Max particle velocity \(v_{p} = a\omega = 60\times10^{-6}\times1200 = 0.072\) m/s.
Wave velocity \(v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{1200}{6} = 200\) m/s.
\[\frac{v_{p}}{v} = \frac{0.072}{200} = 3.6\times10^{-4}.\]

44.subtopic: Satellites, Orbital Motion, and Kepler's Laws

45.subtopic: SHM Energy — Kinetic, Potential, and Total
45.solution:
T.E. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^{2}A^{2}\); K.E. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^{2}(A^{2}-x^{2})\). Given T.E. \(= n\times\)K.E. at \(x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}A\):
\[A^{2} = n(A^{2}-x^{2}) = nA^{2}\left(1 - \frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{n}{4}A^{2} \Rightarrow n = 4.\]

46.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
46.solution: By Lenz's law the induced current in the ring opposes the change in flux, exerting a force on the falling magnet that opposes its motion (upward). The net downward force is reduced, so the acceleration is less than \(g\).

47.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
47.solution: In single-slit diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima and far brighter, so the fringes have unequal width and unequal intensity. The incorrect statement is that the fringes have equal width and equal intensity.

48.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
48.solution: A p-n junction diode conducts only during the half cycles that forward-bias it (half-wave rectification), so across the load a pulsating (unidirectional, not constant) voltage appears.

49.solution: Two oppositely travelling waves of speed \(v = 12\) m/s and frequency \(n\) form a stationary wave with \(\lambda = \dfrac{v}{n} = \dfrac{12}{n}\). Distance between consecutive nodes \(= \dfrac{\lambda}{2} = \dfrac{6}{n}\).

50.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
50.solution:
Induced emf \(|e| = \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(50t^{2} + 4) = 100t\). At \(t = 2\) s, \(|e| = 200\) V.
Current \(I = \dfrac{e}{R} = \dfrac{200}{400} = 0.5\) A.

51.solution: In \(\mathrm{HPO_4^{2-} + H_2O \rightleftharpoons PO_4^{3-} + H_3O^{+}}\), a conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one \(\mathrm{H^{+}}\). Here \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) gains a proton to become \(\mathrm{H_3O^{+}}\), so \(\mathrm{H_3O^{+}}\) (acid) and \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) (base) form one conjugate acid-base pair.

52.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
52.solution: Adenine and guanine (purines) and cytosine (pyrimidine) all carry an \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) (amino) group on the ring. Thymine (pyrimidine) bears two ring carbonyl groups and a methyl group but no \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) attached to the ring. Hence thymine.

53.solution: Histidine has an imidazole ring (a five-membered heterocyclic ring containing two nitrogen atoms) in its side chain \((R)\). Threonine \((\mathrm{CH_3CHOH{-}})\), cysteine \((\mathrm{HSCH_2{-}})\) and valine \((\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}})\) have no heterocyclic ring. Hence histidine.

54.solution: Packing efficiency of an fcc unit cell is \(74\%\), so the volume occupied by the particles \(= 0.74 \times V_{cell} = 0.74 \times 1.6\times 10^{-23} = 1.184\times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
54.stemOverride: Calculate the volume occupied by all particles in fcc unit cell if volume of unit cell is \(1.6 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
54.note: Stem cell volume lost its leading digit in extraction ('.6' \(\to\) intended \(1.6\times10^{-23}\)); restored so \(0.74\times1.6\times10^{-23}=1.184\times10^{-23}\) is reproducible. Key C correct.

55.solution: Molar mass of \(\mathrm{CaCl_2} = 40 + 2(35.5) = 111\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\). Moles \(= 222/111 = 2\ \mathrm{mol}\). Each \(\mathrm{CaCl_2}\) gives \(2\,\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\), so number of \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}} = 2\times 2\times N_A = 4N_A\).

56.solution: Positive deviation arises when solute-solvent interactions are weaker than the solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions. Ethanol-acetone (the acetone disrupts ethanol H-bonding) shows positive deviation. Benzene-toluene is nearly ideal; chloroform-acetone shows negative deviation; phenol-aniline shows negative deviation.

57.solution: In \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\): \(1 + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7\). In \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\): \(y + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +4\). Difference \(= 7 - 4 = 3\).

58.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
58.solution: Work of expansion at constant external pressure \(W = -P_{ext}\,\Delta V = -1\ \mathrm{atm}\,(20 - 15.5)\ \mathrm{dm^3} = -4.5\ \mathrm{dm^3\,atm}\). Converting, \(-4.5 \times 101.325 = -456\ \mathrm{J}\).

59.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
59.solution: For \(\mathrm{2NO + 2H_2 \to N_2 + 2H_2O}\), rate \(= -\tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\). Hence \(\tfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac12\tfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\), which is option B.

61.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
61.solution: Supercritical \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) (and water) are used as green solvents in place of volatile halogenated organic solvents such as \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\), \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}\) and \(\mathrm{CCl_4}\). Hence supercritical \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).

62.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
62.solution: Vapour density \(= \dfrac{\text{molar mass of gas}}{\text{molar mass of } \mathrm{H_2}} = \dfrac{32}{2} = 16\).

63.solution: In both \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) and \(\mathrm{SiCl_4}\) the central atom has 4 bond pairs and no lone pairs, giving the same (tetrahedral) geometry with no lone pair of electrons. Hence option C.

64.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
64.solution: \([\mathrm{Ni(CN)_4}]^{2-}\): \(\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\) is \(\mathrm{[Ar]3d^8}\). The strong-field \(\mathrm{CN^{-}}\) pairs the d-electrons, freeing one \(3d\) orbital, giving \(dsp^2\) hybridization and square planar geometry.

65.subtopic: Group 16 Chalcogens, Oxygen, Sulphur and Ozone
65.solution: In the Maharashtra board structure of disulphuric (pyrosulphuric) acid \(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\), each sulphur atom is shown bonded to oxygen through one \(\mathrm{S{=}O}\) double bond and two \(\mathrm{S{-}O}\) single bonds (the remaining bond being to the \(-\mathrm{OH}\)/bridging oxygen). Hence one double bond and two single bonds.
65.note: Textbook-recall figure question (figure absent from extraction). Per the board's drawn structure of disulphuric acid the keyed answer A (one double + two single S-O bonds per S) is the intended response; retained as keyed.

66.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
66.solution: Lithium, potassium and cesium are Group 1 alkali metals. Beryllium is a Group 2 alkaline earth metal, so it is NOT an alkali metal.

67.subtopic: Polyhalogen Compounds — Freon, DDT, War Gases
67.solution: Mustard gas is \(\mathrm{Cl{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}S{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Cl}\) (bis(2-chloroethyl) sulphide). \(\mathrm{COCl_2}\) is phosgene, \(\mathrm{CCl_3NO_2}\) is chloropicrin, \(\mathrm{CCl_2F_2}\) is a Freon.

68.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
68.solution: For \(r = k[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]\), doubling \([\mathrm{A}]\) while keeping \([\mathrm{B}]\) constant gives \(r' = k(2[\mathrm{A}])[\mathrm{B}] = 2r\). Hence option B.

69.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
69.solution: Standard reduction potentials: \(\mathrm{2H^{+}/H_2}\) \(= 0.00\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{F_2/F^{-}}\) \(= +2.87\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{Li^{+}/Li}\) \(= -3.04\ \mathrm{V}\), \(\mathrm{Cl_2/Cl^{-}}\) \(= +1.36\ \mathrm{V}\). The minimum (most negative) is \(\mathrm{Li^{+} + e^{-} \to Li}\).

70.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
70.solution: A p-type semiconductor is made by doping Ge/Si with a Group 13 (trivalent) element, which creates electron holes. Among the options only boron (B) is Group 13; P, As and Sb are Group 15 (give n-type).

72.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
72.solution: Moles of water \(= 1.8/18 = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}\), vaporised by \(4\ \mathrm{kJ}\). Heat of vaporisation per mole \(= 4/0.1 = 40\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\).

74.solution: A hydrogen-like species has exactly one electron. \(\mathrm{Li^{2+}}\) (2 e\(^-\) removed from 3), \(\mathrm{Be^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{He^{+}}\) each have 1 electron, but \(\mathrm{Li^{+}}\) has 2 electrons, so it is NOT hydrogen-like.

75.solution: Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). Polyacrylonitrile, chloroprene (neoprene) and tetrafluoroethylene (Teflon) are synthetic.

76.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
76.solution: In aqueous medium the combined inductive, steric and solvation effects make secondary methylamine the strongest base among methylamines: \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH_3}\). Hence \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH}\).

77.solution: Aqua \((\mathrm{H_2O})\) is a neutral ligand. Nitrate \((\mathrm{NO_3^{-}})\), cyano \((\mathrm{CN^{-}})\) and iodo \((\mathrm{I^{-}})\) are anionic ligands. Hence aqua.

78.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
78.solution: Owing to the lanthanoid contraction, ionic radius decreases from \(\mathrm{La^{3+}}\) to \(\mathrm{Lu^{3+}}\), so basicity of the hydroxides decreases across the series. \(\mathrm{Lu(OH)_3}\) (smallest cation) is the weakest base.

79.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
79.solution: Of comparable molar mass, an alkane (\(n\)-butane, only weak London forces) boils lowest. Ethers are polar, while alcohols and carboxylic acids have H-bonding and boil highest. So \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}\) has the lowest boiling point.

80.solution: Tropone (cycloheptatrienone) is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound (its tropylium-like ring is aromatic without a benzene ring). Aniline, naphthalene and phenol are benzenoid. Hence tropone.

81.solution: Phenol reacts with aqueous bromine (high reactivity, no catalyst) to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate.

82.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
82.solution: The benzene ring carries \(-\mathrm{COOH}\), \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\) (ortho to \(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) and \(-\mathrm{CHO}\). The senior group \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) makes the parent benzoic acid (\(\mathrm{C1}\)). Numbering to give the lowest locants makes \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\) at C2 and \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) (formyl) at C5, i.e. 5-formyl-2-methylbenzoic acid. Naming with the aldehyde as parent (as in A/B) is wrong because \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) outranks \(-\mathrm{CHO}\); C uses higher locants \(\{3,6\}\).
82.note: Stem figure (image7) read: benzene with CH3, COOH ortho to it, and CHO. Options are text IUPAC names; solved from the figure. figureRefIndex 0 (stem diagram).

83.solution: Glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol, \(\mathrm{HOCH_2{-}CH(OH){-}CH_2OH}\): three carbons, an \(-\mathrm{OH}\) on each, and NO carbon-carbon double bond. Option D matches this (HO-CH2 / CH-OH / CH2-OH, no double bond). A and B contain a \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) double bond (enediols, not glycerol); C is a four-carbon triol (butane-1,2,3-triol). Hence D.
83.note: Options are four bond-line structure figures (option text blank). Read all four: A (image8) = HO-CH2-C(OH)=CH-OH, has a C=C double bond; B (image9) = CH2=C(OH)-CH(OH)2, has a double bond + gem-diol; C (image10) = HO-CH2-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-CH3, a four-carbon triol; D (image11) = HO-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-OH = glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol, no double bond). D is the correct glycerol structure. Attaching the four option figures (genuine 2-D skeletal drawings).

84.solution: \(S_N1\) reactivity follows carbocation stability: \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\). tert-Butyl iodide forms the most stable (tertiary) carbocation, so it is most reactive towards \(S_N1\).

85.solution: Coupling of an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium in dry ether to give an alkylarene (here bromobenzene + bromomethane \(\to\) toluene) is the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

86.subtopic: Nomenclature, Hybridization and Stability of Alkenes
86.solution: Structural isomers of \(\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}\) alkenes: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, and 2-methylbut-2-ene = 5 (counting structural isomers, ignoring cis/trans). Hence 5.

87.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
87.solution: \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode}\). Ni is reduced (cathode), Al is oxidised (anode): \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = (-0.25) - (-1.66) = +1.41\ \mathrm{V}\).

88.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
88.solution: Wurtz reaction of \(\mathrm{C_2H_5Cl}\) and \(\mathrm{C_3H_7Cl}\) with Na gives three coupled alkanes: ethane+ethyl \(\to\) butane (\(\mathrm{C_4}\)), ethyl+propyl \(\to\) pentane (\(\mathrm{C_5}\)), propyl+propyl \(\to\) hexane (\(\mathrm{C_6}\)). Propane (\(\mathrm{C_3}\)) is NOT formed.

89.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation

90.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
90.solution: Coagulation is brought about by electrophoresis, by mixing two oppositely charged sols, and by boiling. Adding excess of the dispersion medium (solvent) merely dilutes the sol and does NOT cause coagulation. Hence option B.

92.subtopic: Industrial Processes, Minerals, Hydrogen Compounds and Alloys
92.solution: In the water-gas shift reaction \(\mathrm{CO + H_2O \rightleftharpoons CO_2 + H_2}\), carried out at about \(500^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to enrich the hydrogen, the catalyst used is \(\mathrm{Fe{-}Cr}\) (iron oxide-chromium oxide).

93.solution: Hydroboration-oxidation adds \(-\mathrm{OH}\) with anti-Markovnikov orientation (boron, then OH, on the less substituted/terminal carbon). For but-1-ene \((\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH{=}CH_2})\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) goes to the terminal carbon, giving butan-1-ol.

94.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
94.solution: Azo coupling is the reaction of an arene diazonium salt with a reactive aromatic compound (phenol or aromatic amine) to give an azo dye \((\mathrm{Ar{-}N{=}N{-}Ar'})\). Option B, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl + C_6H_5OH}\) (under mild alkaline conditions), gives \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene, i.e. azo coupling.

95.solution: Gallic acid (3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoic acid) is obtained from Indian gooseberry (amla) and gall nuts. Clove gives eugenol, wintergreen gives methyl salicylate, citrus fruits give citric/ascorbic acid.

96.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
96.solution: \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = \sum\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{reactants})\). With \(\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\mathrm{O_2})=0\): \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = [(-394) + 2(-286)] - [(-75)] = -394 - 572 + 75 = -891\ \mathrm{kJ}\).

97.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
97.solution: Dry ice \((\mathrm{CO_2})\) with \(\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}\) gives \(\mathrm{CH_3COOMgBr}\) (A); acid work-up \((\mathrm{H_3O^{+}})\) gives \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), ethanoic acid (B).

98.solution: Buna-N (nitrile rubber, a copolymer of buta-1,3-diene and acrylonitrile) is oil- and abrasion-resistant and is used for shoe soles, hoses and gaskets. Hence Buna-N.

99.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life

100.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
100.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Mg(s) \to Mg^{2+}(0.01\,M) + 2e^{-}}\), the oxidation electrode potential uses \(E^{\circ}_{ox} = +2.37\ \mathrm{V}\): \(E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}] = +2.37 - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log(10^{-2}) = +2.37 - (0.0296)(-2) = +2.37 + 0.0592 = +2.4292\ \mathrm{V}\).

101.solution: Separating, \(\dfrac{1}{y+1}\,dy=\dfrac{-\cos x}{2+\sin x}\,dx\). Integrating: \(\log(y+1)=-\log(2+\sin x)+c\). At \(x=0,\ y=1\): \(\log 2=-\log 2+c\Rightarrow c=\log 4\). So \(y+1=\dfrac{4}{2+\sin x}\). At \(x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\): \(y=\dfrac{4}{3}-1=\dfrac13\).

103.solution: From \(|\bar a+\bar b|^2+|\bar a+\bar c|^2=8\): \(4+2(\bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c)=8\Rightarrow \bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c=2\). Then \(|\bar a+3\bar b|^2+|\bar a+3\bar c|^2=20+6(\bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c)=20+12=32\).

105.subtopic: Section Formula, Concurrency, Foot of Perpendicular, and Distance
105.solution: Distance of \(ax+by+c=0\) from origin \(=\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\). (A) \(\dfrac4{5}=0.8\); (B) \(\dfrac5{\sqrt{13}}\approx1.39\); (C) \(\dfrac{12}{5}=2.4\); (D) \(\dfrac3{\sqrt{29}}\approx0.557\). The least is option (D).

106.solution: \([p\wedge\sim r]\to(\sim r\wedge q)\equiv F\Rightarrow p\wedge\sim r\equiv T\) and \(\sim r\wedge q\equiv F\). So \(p\equiv T,\ r\equiv F\); with \(\sim r\equiv T\), \(q\equiv F\). Check (D): \(\sim(r\vee q)\to\sim p=\sim(F\vee F)\to\sim T=T\to F\equiv F\).

107.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
107.solution: Let \(\bar d=p\hat i+q\hat j+r\hat k\). Coplanarity \([\bar b\ \bar c\ \bar d]=0\) gives \(p+q+r=0\); \(\bar a\cdot\bar d=0\) gives \(p-q=0\Rightarrow p=q\). Option (D) \(\dfrac{\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k}{\sqrt6}\) satisfies both (\(1+1-2=0\), \(p=q=1\)) and is a unit vector.

108.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
108.solution: Cosine rule: \(a^2+b^2-c^2=2ab\cos C\); squaring and using \(a^4+b^4+c^4=2a^2c^2+2b^2c^2\) gives \(2a^2b^2=4a^2b^2\cos^2 C\Rightarrow\cos^2 C=\dfrac12\Rightarrow\cos C=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\). The only matching option is \(C=135^\circ\).

111.solution: Both lines have direction \((2,3,4)\), so they are parallel; the square's side equals the distance between them. \((\bar r_2-\bar r_1)=(-1,3,-4)\); \((\bar r_2-\bar r_1)\times\bar d=(24,-4,-9)\), magnitude \(\sqrt{673}\); \(|\bar d|=\sqrt{29}\). Side \(=\dfrac{\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}\), so perimeter \(=\dfrac{4\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}\) units.

112.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
112.solution: By Napier's analogy, \(\tan\left(\dfrac{B-C}2\right)=\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}\cot\dfrac A2\). Comparing with \(x\cot\dfrac A2\) gives \(x=\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}\).

113.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

114.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
114.solution: The equation contains \(\log\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)\), so it cannot be written as a polynomial in the derivatives. Hence the degree is not defined.

115.solution: Sum of squares of distances from the three axes \(=(y^2+z^2)+(x^2+z^2)+(x^2+y^2)=2(x^2+y^2+z^2)=324\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+z^2=162\). Distance from origin \(=\sqrt{162}=9\sqrt2\).

116.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
116.solution: For \(i=0,1,\dots,49\): \(\dfrac12\le\dfrac12+\dfrac i{100}<1\Rightarrow\) floor \(=0\). For \(i=50,\dots,99\): \(1\le\dfrac12+\dfrac i{100}<2\Rightarrow\) floor \(=1\), giving 50 terms. Total \(=50\).

117.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions
117.solution: \(3x=2y=-z\Rightarrow\dfrac x2=\dfrac y3=\dfrac z{-6}\); \(-x=6y=-4z\Rightarrow\dfrac x{-12}=\dfrac y2=\dfrac z{-3}\). \(a_1a_2+b_1b_2+c_1c_2=2(-12)+3(2)+(-6)(-3)=-24+6+18=0\). Lines are perpendicular, so the angle is \(\dfrac\pi2\).

118.solution: \(y+\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy)=x(\sin x+\log x)\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x(\sin x+\log x)\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac2x y=\sin x+\log x\). I.F. \(=x^2\). Then \(yx^2=\int(x^2\sin x+x^2\log x)\,dx=-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x+\dfrac{x^3}3\log x-\dfrac{x^3}9+c\). Dividing by \(x^2\): \(y=-\cos x+\dfrac2x\sin x+\dfrac2{x^2}\cos x+\dfrac x3\log x-\dfrac x9+\dfrac c{x^2}\).

119.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
119.solution: \(xy-x+y-1=(x+1)(y-1)=0\), so the lines meet at \((-1,1)\). For concurrency, \(x+ky-3=0\) passes through it: \(-1+k-3=0\Rightarrow k=4\).

120.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters

121.solution: (A) sum of cube roots of unity is \(0\neq1\), so the conjunction is F. (B) \(11>10\) (T) iff \(10<10\) (F): \(T\leftrightarrow F\equiv F\). (C) \(x^2-3x+2=0\) has \(x=1,2\in\mathbb N\) and an odd \(n\) exists: \(T\wedge T\equiv T\). (D) \(3+i\) is complex (T) or \(\sqrt2+\sqrt3=\sqrt5\) (F): \(T\vee F\equiv T\). True statements are (C) and (D).

122.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

123.solution: \(\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\Rightarrow\log\left(\dfrac{P}{40000}\right)=kt\). From \(t=20,\ P=80000\): \(20k=\log2\). The further 40 years means \(t=60\): \(\log\left(\dfrac{P}{40000}\right)=3\log2\Rightarrow P=40000\cdot8=320000\).

124.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
124.solution: Coplanarity \(\Rightarrow\begin{vmatrix}m&m&n\\1&0&1\\n&n&p\end{vmatrix}=0\Rightarrow -mn-mp+mn+n^2=0\Rightarrow n^2=mp\). Hence \(m,n,p\) are in G.P.

125.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
125.solution: Terms run \(\sin^2 5^\circ,\dots,\sin^2 90^\circ\) (step \(5^\circ\), 18 terms). Pairing \(\sin^2\theta+\sin^2(90^\circ-\theta)=1\) gives 8 pairs \((5,85),\dots,(40,50)=8\); the middle term \(\sin^2 45^\circ=\dfrac12\) and \(\sin^2 90^\circ=1\). Total \(=8+\dfrac12+1=\dfrac{19}2\).

126.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines

128.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
128.solution: By \(x\to\pi-x\), \(2I=\pi\int_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x}=\pi\int_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}(\sec^2 x-\sec x\tan x)\,dx=\pi[\tan x-\sec x]_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}=\pi[(-\sqrt3+2)-(\sqrt3-2)]=2\pi(2-\sqrt3)\). Hence \(I=\pi(2-\sqrt3)\).

130.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms

131.solution: \(\cos2x-\cos2\alpha=2(\cos^2 x-\cos^2\alpha)=2(\cos x-\cos\alpha)(\cos x+\cos\alpha)\). So \(\int\dfrac{\cos2x-\cos2\alpha}{\cos x-\cos\alpha}\,dx=2\int(\cos x+\cos\alpha)\,dx=2\sin x+2x\cos\alpha+c\).

132.solution: Choose 12 of 21 for the first table and arrange round both tables: \(\binom{21}{12}\times11!\times8!=\dfrac{21!}{12!\,9!}\times11!\times8!=\dfrac{21!}{12\cdot9}=\dfrac{35}{9}\times19!\).

133.solution: Area \(=\dfrac12|\bar d_1\times\bar d_2|\) where \(\bar d_1=2\bar a-\bar b,\ \bar d_2=4\bar a-5\bar b\). \(\bar d_1\times\bar d_2=-6(\bar a\times\bar b)\), and \(|\bar a\times\bar b|=\sin45^\circ=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\). Area \(=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac6{\sqrt2}=\dfrac3{\sqrt2}\) sq. units.

135.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

136.subtopic: Algebraic Equations, Locus, and Cube Roots
136.solution: \(\left|\dfrac{z+i}{z-i}\right|=\sqrt3\Rightarrow x^2+(y+1)^2=3[x^2+(y-1)^2]\Rightarrow x^2+(y-2)^2=3\). This is a circle with centre \((0,2)\) and radius \(\sqrt3\).

137.solution: Writing \(\dfrac{2x^2+3}{(x^2-1)(x^2-4)}=\dfrac{11/3}{x^2-4}-\dfrac{5/3}{x^2-1}\) and integrating gives \(\dfrac{11}{12}\log\left|\dfrac{x-2}{x+2}\right|+\dfrac56\log\left|\dfrac{x+1}{x-1}\right|+c\). So \(a=\dfrac{11}{12},\ b=\dfrac56\) and \(a+b=\dfrac{11}{12}+\dfrac{10}{12}=\dfrac{21}{12}\).

139.subtopic: Basic Probability — Events, Conditional, and Complement

141.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition

142.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
142.solution: Tangent slope \(m=-\dfrac1{-4/3}=\dfrac34\). For \(\dfrac{x^2}{20}-\dfrac{y^2}5=1\): \(y=mx\pm\sqrt{a^2m^2-b^2}=\dfrac34x\pm\sqrt{20\cdot\tfrac9{16}-5}=\dfrac34x\pm\dfrac52\). For one tangent, x-intercept \(=\dfrac{10}3\) (\(y=0\)) and y-intercept \(=-\dfrac52\) (\(x=0\)). This matches option (B).

143.solution: Coplanarity determinant gives \(-2(k^2-4)=0\Rightarrow k=\pm2\). For \(k=2\) the containing plane is \(y-z+1=0\); for \(k=-2\) it is \(y+z+1=0\). Hence \(y\pm z+1=0\).

144.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
144.solution: For \(y=mx+c\) tangent to \(y^2=4ax\) (here \(a=1\)), \(c=\dfrac am\). With \(c=3\): \(3=\dfrac1m\Rightarrow m=\dfrac13\).

145.solution: At \((\sqrt3,1)\) on \(x^2+y^2=4\): tangent slope \(=-\sqrt3\), so tangent \(\sqrt3x+y=4\) meets the X-axis at \(\left(\dfrac4{\sqrt3},0\right)\); the normal passes through the origin \((0,0)\). Triangle area \(=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\cdot1=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\) sq. units.

146.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

149.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
149.solution: Let \(y=16^{\sin^2 x}\); then \(16^{\cos^2 x}=\dfrac{16}y\) and \(y+\dfrac{16}y=10\Rightarrow y^2-10y+16=0\Rightarrow y=8\) or \(2\). So \(2^{4\sin^2 x}=2^3\) or \(2^1\Rightarrow\sin^2 x=\dfrac34\) or \(\dfrac14\Rightarrow\sin x=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt3}2,\ \pm\dfrac12\). In \([0,2\pi]\) this gives \(x=\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{2\pi}3,\dfrac{4\pi}3,\dfrac{5\pi}3,\dfrac\pi6,\dfrac{5\pi}6,\dfrac{7\pi}6,\dfrac{11\pi}6\) — 8 solutions.
149.note: Source had status no_answer_key (akAnswer null). Independently derived: 8 solutions = option A.

150.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
150.solution: Point \((2,1,-2)\) lies in \(x+3y-\alpha z+\beta=0\): \(2+3+2\alpha+\beta=0\Rightarrow2\alpha+\beta=-5\). Direction \((3,-5,2)\perp\) normal \((1,3,-\alpha)\): \(3-15-2\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha=-6\), so \(\beta=7\). Hence \(\beta-\alpha=7-(-6)=13\).
